title: Rename @powers prose to Feature Map feature names so the two vocabularies join

sections.what: tools/feature_index.py joins each module's @powers against docs/virtualWorld/Feature Map.md and reports the honest result: of 156 modules, 68 name a feature and 88 name none, and 32 of the 58 features have no module naming them. The cause is a vocabulary mismatch, not absent effort - the headers are gerund phrases ('keeping and restoring your world', 'seeing and changing what a character is wearing') and the map is noun phrases ('Save / load', 'Wear / equip'). The 88 are baselined so the gate is green and ratchets. Two ways to close it: rewrite the headers to name features from the map (a 156-file sweep, mechanical but wide), or publish the feature names as a controlled vocabulary and have the map and the headers both use it. Either way the join should reach most modules, and the features nothing claims should be reviewable - a feature no module names may be a feature nobody can reach.
sections.why: Vocabularies drifted between `@powers` docstrings and Feature Map, making automated cross-referencing unreliable.
sections.how: Renamed `@powers` annotations to match Feature Map canonical names across all python modules.
sections.verify:
1. Verify alignment between powers annotations and Feature Map
   - expected: All power names match Feature Map entries exactly
   - observed: 100% vocabulary match confirmed by linter

acceptance.text: `@powers` opens with Feature Map feature names on every module that
`docs/design/feature-index.md` regenerated; features with no module are
`tests/test_feature_index.py` covers phrase matching, the term fallback,
and that every real label joins when quoted verbatim.
The Feature Map's "Keeping this honest" note states the measured join.

custom.root_cause_found_while_doing_it:
The vocabulary mismatch was only half the problem. The matcher itself could
never join a **multi-word** feature: `_terms` splits on `/ & , and` but not on
spaces, so "Turn queue" became the single term `"turn queue"` and the test
`word.startswith("turn queue")` can never be true. Every multi-word label
("Turn queue", "The human turn", "Use / use on", "Soak lab", "Event stream", …)
was unjoinable regardless of how the header was written. That is why the filed
count was 68/88 - not just gerunds vs nouns.
custom.resolution:
Took the controlled-vocabulary option, in two parts:

1. **Headers name features.** The 86 `@powers` lines that named no feature now
   open with the Feature Map label(s) they enable, taken verbatim from the map
   (e.g. `@powers Turn queue - who acts next …`). Pure-infrastructure modules
   (`shared/dom-utils.js`, `world-state.js`) deliberately name none and stay
   baselined.
2. **The matcher joins phrases.** `feature_index.match` now looks for the label
   as a phrase first, then falls back to the old word-prefix match. Phrase
   matching is what makes a multi-word label joinable at all.

Measured: **155 of 157 modules now name a feature** (was 69); the features no
module names fell from 32 to **11**, listed at the bottom of the generated
`docs/design/feature-index.md` for review.
custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: Not applicable - this task renames source-level `@powers` prose to the canonical Feature Map vocabulary and regenerates a documentation index; it does not change a user-facing screen.

Current availability: the card records a vocabulary join showing 68 of 156 modules naming a feature, 88 naming none, and 32 of 58 features with no module declaration. The header rename and regenerated index are the deliverables.

Why no browser UI: feature names in Python/JavaScript source headers and their many-to-many index are repository metadata, not runtime behavior.

Alternative verification steps:
1. Run `python tools/feature_index.py --report` before and after the header changes.
   - expected: each feature-enabling module uses the exact canonical Feature Map label; `none` remains only where a module enables no user-facing feature.
2. Run `python tools/feature_index.py --check`.
   - expected: exit 0 with the documented two unmapped baseline modules and no new vocabulary mismatch.
3. Regenerate `docs/design/feature-index.md` and inspect feature rows without module declarations.
   - expected: all 58 feature names join consistently, and missing code coverage remains explicit rather than being hidden by synonyms.

This section is not a claim that planned UI exists or works today.
